text: Consider a database schema consisting of the following relations for recording information on the clients of a stock broking firm: Clients (cIno, name, phone) Stocks (scode, sname, price, dividend, eps) BuySell (clno. trdate, trtype, scode, qty, price) StocksOwned (clno, scode, totalgty, totalcost, currval) A tuple in the Clients table consists of a unique client number, name and phone number. Each tuple of Stocks table contains unique stock code, stock name, the current price of a share, dividend per share, and earning per share (eps). Each transaction of a client which may be a buy or a sell of a stock is recorded a tuple in the BuySell table. It contains the client number, transaction date and time, type of transaction (B for buy or S for sell), stock code, number of shares (qty) and price per share for the transaction. The StocksOwned table contains a tuple for each stock a client currently owns, along with the total quantity of the stock, the total cost of purchasing the stock, and its current value. The primary key of each table is underlined.
